narratives.text: The Atlas engineering manager should first find where the extra cycle time (3.2 to 4.5 days) accumulates, starting with PR review, which rose from 10 to 16.5 hours. Check reviewer load and availability, then agree a review turnaround target and rotation for order-api and storefront-ui. Success is PR review time at or below 11 hours by week 22. P1 is proportionate: cycle time, lead time and review time are all trending upward, and planned work may ship later if this continues.

narratives.text: The engineering director should run a short practice review with Phoenix on what changed in testing, review and release habits since week 5, then publish the findings and share them with Atlas. Phoenix raised test coverage from 64.7% to 76.6% and automated tests from 82.8% to 91.9%, while rework rate fell from 10.8% to 9.7%. Success by week 22 means Phoenix keeps its improvement and adopting teams' quality trend stops deteriorating. P2 fits a low-cost knowledge share, not an urgent fix.

narratives.author: risk-narrator
narratives.text: Atlas quality is deteriorating: test coverage fell from 72% to 63.2% and automated tests from 80.4% to 75.7% since week 8, while defects rose from 6 to 12 (+100%) and rework rate from 8.3% to 12.8%. This may mean more defects reach users and more unplanned rework competes with roadmap work. One possibility worth checking is that falling coverage and automated testing may be letting more defects through, as coverage changes preceded defect changes by 1 week; this is a lagged association, not proof.

narratives.text: On the Data platform, change failure rate rose from 5.4% to 27.1% and rollback rate from 1.1% to 25.9%, while failed deployments went from 0.5 to 6 and incidents from 1 to 5.5 since week 11. This means more failed releases and customer-facing incidents on Data services. One possibility worth checking is whether deployment-related changes are associated with the incident rise: change-attributed incidents went from 50% to 80% in post-incident reviews, though this shift is not statistically significant (p=0.097).
